description: This figure is a single rendered table (Table III) with no micrographs, curves or schematics. The header row, printed in bold with a horizontal rule beneath it, reads from left to right: "% Si", "% P", "Heat treatment", "Hardness (BHN)", "Average CVN energy (ft-lbs)", "Average CVN energy (J)" and "Test temperature (°C)". Three data rows follow, all with the Heat treatment entry "Solution treated" and the Test temperature entry "25" °C, i.e. all specimens were tested at 25 °C in the solution-treated condition. The table is organised around nominally Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steel with different phosphorus levels, as stated in the caption. Row 1: % Si = 1.07, % P = 0.07, hardness 242 ± 6 BHN, CVN energy 21 ± 4 ft-lbs = 28 J. Row 2: % Si = 1.01, % P = 0.006, hardness 194 ± 2 BHN, CVN energy 92 ± 1 ft-lbs = 124 J. Row 3: % Si = 1.07, % P = 0.001, hardness 192 ± 10 BHN, CVN energy 147 ± 17 ft-lbs = 199 J. The table therefore demonstrates that reducing phosphorus from 0.07 to 0.006 and then 0.001 wt.% drops hardness from 242 to ~192 BHN while raising Charpy V-notch impact energy about sevenfold, from 28 J to 199 J, at the same test temperature. No graphical panels, scale bars or plotted axes are present; the caption explicitly names Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C as the nominal composition.

observations.observation: The figure is a table (Table III), not a plot: it contains a bold seven-column header and three data rows, with no axes, curves or images.
The columns are labelled '% Si', '% P', 'Heat treatment', 'Hardness (BHN)', 'Average CVN energy (ft-lbs)', 'Average CVN energy (J)' and 'Test temperature (°C)'.
The caption states the table reports the solution-treated CVN breaking energy for nominally Fe-30Mn-9Al-1Si-0.9C steels with different amounts of phosphorus.
Row 1: 1.07 % Si, 0.07 % P, solution treated, hardness 242 ± 6 BHN, 21 ± 4 ft-lbs (28 J), tested at 25 °C.
Row 2: 1.01 % Si, 0.006 % P, solution treated, hardness 194 ± 2 BHN, 92 ± 1 ft-lbs (124 J), tested at 25 °C.
Row 3: 1.07 % Si, 0.001 % P, solution treated, hardness 192 ± 10 BHN, 147 ± 17 ft-lbs (199 J), tested at 25 °C.
All three heats were given the same 'Solution treated' heat treatment and were all tested at 25 °C, so phosphorus level and Si level differ while test temperature and treatment are held constant.
Hardness decreases as phosphorus decreases: 242 ± 6 BHN at 0.07 % P versus 194 ± 2 BHN at 0.006 % P and 192 ± 10 BHN at 0.001 % P.
Average CVN energy increases strongly as phosphorus decreases: 28 J at 0.07 % P, 124 J at 0.006 % P and 199 J at 0.001 % P at 25 °C.
The two CVN energy columns are consistent with a unit conversion: 21 ft-lbs → 28 J, 92 ft-lbs → 124 J and 147 ft-lbs → 199 J correspond to the same values expressed in the two unit systems.
No scale bars, magnification markers, error-bar plots or graphical data points are present in the figure; only tabulated values with ± uncertainties.
